Kikuyu: Nĩ niĩ Jakubu, ndungata ya Ngai na ya Mwathani Jesũ Kristũ, Ndĩramwandĩkĩra inyuĩ a mĩhĩrĩga ĩrĩa ikũmi na ĩĩrĩ mũhurunjĩtwo thĩ yothe: Nĩndamũgeithia.
English: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are in the Dispersion: Greetings.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, rĩrĩa rĩothe mwakorwo nĩ magerio ma mĩthemba mĩingĩ-rĩ, tuagai atĩ ũguo nĩ gĩkeno gĩtheri.
English: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,

Kikuyu: tondũ nĩmũũĩ atĩ kũgerio kwa wĩtĩkio wanyu kũrehaga gũkirĩrĩria.
English: knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.

Kikuyu: Rekei gũkirĩrĩria kwanyu kũrute wĩra wakuo, nĩgeetha mũtuĩke andũ aagĩrĩru kũna na agima, mũtarĩ na ũndũ mwagĩte.
English: Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, mũndũ wanyu angĩkorwo aagĩte ũũgĩ-rĩ, nĩahooe Ngai, ũrĩa ũheaga andũ othe na ũtaana, na atarĩ na ũũru ngoro, nake nĩekũheo ũũgĩ ũcio.
English: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩa ekũhooya-rĩ, nĩahooe etĩkĩtie, na ndagathanganie, tondũ mũndũ ũrĩa ũthanganagia ahaana ta ikũmbĩ rĩa iria inene, rĩrĩa rĩhurutagwo nĩ rũhuho na rĩkarũgarũũgio.
English: But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ ũcio ndageciirie atĩ nĩakaheo kĩndũ o nakĩ nĩ Mwathani;
English: For that man shouldn’t think that he will receive anything from the Lord.

Kikuyu: ũcio nĩ mũndũ wa ngoro igĩrĩ, ũtarĩ hĩndĩ akindagĩria maũndũ-inĩ mothe marĩa ekaga.
English: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

Kikuyu: Mũrũ kana mwarĩ wa Ithe witũ ũrĩa wĩnyiihagia aagĩrĩirwo nĩ kwĩraha nĩ ũndũ nĩatũũgĩrĩtio.
English: Let the brother in humble circumstances glory in his high position;

Kikuyu: No ũrĩa mũtongu nĩerahage nĩ ũndũ wa kũnyiihio gwake, tondũ agaathira ta ihũa rĩa gĩthaka.
English: and the rich, in that he is made humble, because like the flower in the grass, he will pass away.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo riũa rĩrathaga rĩrĩ na ũrugarĩ mũhiũ wa gũcina narĩo rĩkahoohia mũmera; nakĩo kĩro kĩaguo gĩgaitĩka na ũthaka waguo ũkanangwo. Ũguo no taguo mũndũ ũrĩa mũtongu akaahwererekera o akĩrutaga wĩra wake.
English: For the sun arises with the scorching wind and withers the grass; and the flower in it falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So the rich man will also fade away in his pursuits.

Kikuyu: Kũrathimwo-rĩ, nĩ mũndũ ũrĩa ũũmagĩrĩria rĩrĩa ekũgerio, tondũ aatooria magerio, nĩakaheo thũmbĩ ya muoyo ĩrĩa Ngai erĩire arĩa mamwendete.
English: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa mwagerio, mũndũ o naũ ndakanoige atĩrĩ, “Ngai nĩarangeria.” Nĩgũkorwo Ngai ndangĩhota kũgerio nĩ ũũru, o nake mwene ndageragia mũndũ o na ũrĩkũ;
English: Let no man say when he is tempted, “I am tempted by God,” for God can’t be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.

Kikuyu: no rĩrĩ, mũndũ nĩkũgerio ageragio hĩndĩ ĩrĩa ekũguucĩrĩrio na akaheenererio nĩ merirĩria make mooru.
English: But each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust and enticed.

Kikuyu: Namo merirĩria marĩkia kũgĩa nda, maciaraga mehia; namo mehia hĩndĩ ĩrĩa maakũra biũ, magaciara gĩkuũ.
English: Then the lust, when it has conceived, bears sin. The sin, when it is full grown, produces death.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ inyuĩ nyenda mũno-rĩ, mũtikanaheenio.
English: Don’t be deceived, my beloved brothers.

Kikuyu: Kĩheo gĩothe kĩega na gĩkinyanĩru kiumaga igũrũ, gĩikũrũkĩte kuuma kũrĩ Ithe wa motheri ma igũrũ, ũrĩa ũtagarũrũkaga ta ciĩruru iria igarũrũkaga.
English: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation nor turning shadow.

Kikuyu: Nĩwe watũciarire nĩ kwenda na ũndũ wa ũhoro-ũrĩa-wa-ma, nĩguo tũtuĩke ta maciaro ma mbere ma indo ciothe iria ombire.
English: Of his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ inyuĩ nyenda mũno, menyai ũũ: O mũndũ nĩahiũhage gũthikĩrĩria, no ndakahiũhage kwaria o na kana kũrakara,
English: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;

Kikuyu: nĩgũkorwo marakara ma mũndũ matirehaga mũtũũrĩre wa ũthingu ũrĩa Ngai endaga.
English: for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio-rĩ, eheriai maũndũ mothe marĩ magigi, na ũũru ũrĩa ũkĩrĩrĩirie kũingĩha, na mwĩnyiihĩtie, mwĩtĩkĩre kiugo kĩrĩa kĩhaandĩtwo thĩinĩ wanyu, o kĩrĩa kĩngĩmũhonokia.
English: Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.

Kikuyu: Mũtigatuĩke o a gũthikagĩrĩria kiugo tu, no tuĩkai a gwĩka ũrĩa kiugĩte, nĩguo mũtikeheenie inyuĩ ene.
English: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ o wothe ũthikagĩrĩria kiugo no ndekaga ũrĩa kiugĩte-rĩ, ahaana ta mũndũ ũrĩa wĩroraga ũthiũ na gĩcicio,
English: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;

Kikuyu: na thuutha wa kwĩrora, agethiĩra na akariganĩrwo o narua nĩ ũrĩa ahaana.
English: for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.

Kikuyu: No mũndũ ũrĩa ũroraga wega watho ũrĩa mũkinyanĩru kũna ũrĩa ũheanaga wĩyathi, na agathiĩ na mbere gwĩka ũguo, atekũriganĩrwo nĩ ũrĩa aiguĩte no akawĩkaga-rĩ, ũcio nĩarĩrathimagĩrwo maũndũ marĩa ekaga.
English: But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ o wothe angĩĩtua mũndũ wa ndini no aremwo nĩ gwatha rũrĩmĩ rwake-rĩ, mũndũ ũcio nĩ kwĩheenia eheenagia, na ũndini wake nĩ wa tũhũ.
English: If anyone among you thinks himself to be religious while he doesn’t bridle his tongue, but deceives his heart, this man’s religion is worthless.

Kikuyu: Ũndini ũrĩa Ngai Ithe witũ etĩkagĩra atĩ nĩ mũtheru na ndũrĩ na mahĩtia nĩ ũyũ: nĩ kũroraga ciana cia ngoriai na atumia a ndigwa hĩndĩ ĩrĩa marĩ mathĩĩna-inĩ mao, na ningĩ mũndũ etheemage ndagathũkio nĩ maũndũ ma gũkũ thĩ.
English: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, ta etĩkia thĩinĩ wa Mwathani witũ Jesũ Kristũ, o we ũrĩa ũrĩ riiri-rĩ, tigagai gũthutũkanagia andũ nĩ ũndũ wa maũthĩ mao.
English: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.

Kikuyu: Tondũ-rĩ, ĩ hihi kũngĩũka mũndũ kĩũngano- inĩ kĩanyu ekĩrĩte gĩcũhĩ gĩa thahabu na nguo njega, na gũũke mũndũ mũthĩĩni ũtehumbĩte nguo njega-rĩ,
English: For if a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, comes into your synagogue, and a poor man in filthy clothing also comes in,

Kikuyu: na inyuĩ mũhe ũcio wĩhumbĩte nguo njega gĩtĩĩo, mũmwĩre atĩrĩ, “Haha harĩ na gĩtĩ kĩega gĩa gũikarĩra,” no mwĩre mũndũ ũcio mũthĩĩni atĩrĩ, “Wee rũgama harĩa,” kana, “Ikara haha magũrũ- inĩ makwa,”
English: and you pay special attention to him who wears the fine clothing and say, “Sit here in a good place;” and you tell the poor man, “Stand there,” or “Sit by my footstool”

Kikuyu: githĩ mũtiagĩthutũkania inyuĩ ene, na mwatuĩka atuanĩri ciira marĩ na meciiria mooru?
English: haven’t you shown partiality among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ inyuĩ nyenda mũno, ta thikĩrĩriai: Githĩ Ngai ndathuurĩte arĩa monagwo marĩ athĩĩni gũkũ thĩ nĩguo matuĩke itonga ũhoro-inĩ wa wĩtĩkio na magaĩrwo ũthamaki ũrĩa erĩire arĩa mamwendete?
English: Listen, my beloved brothers. Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom which he promised to those who love him?

Kikuyu: No inyuĩ nĩ mũnyararaga arĩa athĩĩni. Githĩ ti itonga imũhinyagĩrĩria? Githĩ ti o mamũtwaraga igooti-inĩ na hinya?
English: But you have dishonored the poor man. Don’t the rich oppress you and personally drag you before the courts?

Kikuyu: Ningĩ githĩ ti o macambagia rĩĩtwa rĩrĩa rĩrĩ gĩtĩĩo, o rĩu rĩa ũrĩa mũrĩ ake?
English: Don’t they blaspheme the honorable name by which you are called?

Kikuyu: Angĩkorwo nĩmũhingagia watho ũrĩa mũtue nĩ mũthamaki ũrĩa wandĩkĩtwo Maandĩko-inĩ atĩrĩ, “Enda mũndũ ũrĩa ũngĩ o ta ũrĩa wĩyendete wee mwene,” nĩmwĩkaga wega.
English: However, if you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.

Kikuyu: No angĩkorwo mũtĩĩagĩra andũ maũthĩ-rĩ, nĩ kwĩhia mwĩhagia na mũrĩ atuĩre nĩ watho atĩ mũrĩ aagarari watho.
English: But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo ũrĩa wothe ũhingagia watho wothe, no akahĩngwo nĩ kaũndũ o kamwe ka guo, mũndũ ũcio nĩagararĩte watho wothe.
English: For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet stumbles in one point, he has become guilty of all.

Kikuyu: Tondũ ũrĩa woigire atĩ, “Ndũkanatharanie,” nowe woigire atĩ, “Ndũkanoragane.” Rĩu-rĩ, ũngĩaga gũtharania no ũragane-rĩ, wee nĩũtuĩkĩte mwagarari wa watho.
English: For he who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not commit murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.

Kikuyu: Aragiai na mwĩkage maũndũ manyu o ta mũrĩ arĩa magaatuĩrwo ciira nĩ watho ũrĩa ũheanaga wĩyathi,
English: So speak and so do as men who are to be judged by the law of freedom.

Kikuyu: tondũ mũndũ ũrĩa ũtuanĩire ciira atekũiguanĩra tha-rĩ, ũcio nake agaatuĩrwo ciira atekũiguĩrwo tha. Nacio tha nĩitooragia ũtuanĩri wa ciira!
English: For judgment is without mercy to him who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, gũkĩrĩ na uumithio ũrĩkũ mũndũ angiuga atĩ arĩ na wĩtĩkio, no ndarĩ na ciĩko? Wĩtĩkio ũcio wakĩmũhonokia?
English: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him?

Kikuyu: Mũrũ wa Ithe witũ kana mwarĩ wa Ithe witũ angĩkorwo ndarĩ na nguo cia kwĩhumba, kana irio cia kũrĩa o mũthenya,
English: And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food,

Kikuyu: nake ũmwe wanyu amwĩre atĩrĩ, “Thiĩ na wega; gĩa na ũrugarĩ na ũrĩe wega,” no ndarĩ ũndũ aamũteithia naguo mabataro-inĩ make ma mwĩrĩ- rĩ, ũndũ ũcio ũkĩrĩ na uumithio ũrĩkũ?
English: and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?

Kikuyu: Ũguo no taguo wĩtĩkio mũtheri ũtarĩ na ciĩko ũhaana, nĩ mũkuũ guo mwene.
English: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.

Kikuyu: No mũndũ no oige atĩrĩ, “Wee-rĩ, ũrĩ na wĩtĩkio; na niĩ ndĩ na ciĩko.” Nyonia wĩtĩkio waku ũrĩa ũtarĩ na ciĩko, na niĩ nĩngũkuonia wĩtĩkio wakwa na ũndũ wa ũrĩa njĩkaga.
English: Yes, a man will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works.

Kikuyu: Wee nĩwĩtĩkĩtie atĩ Ngai no ũmwe. Ũguo nĩ wega! O nacio ndaimono nĩciĩtĩkĩtie ũguo, na ikainaina.
English: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe—and shudder.

Kikuyu: Wee kĩrimũ gĩkĩ, nĩ ũira ũrakĩenda wa kuonania atĩ wĩtĩkio ũtarĩ na ciĩko nĩ wa tũhũ?
English: But do you want to know, vain man, that faith apart from works is dead?

Kikuyu: Githĩ Iburahĩmu, ithe witũ wa tene, ndaatuirwo mũthingu nĩ ũndũ wa ũrĩa eekire rĩrĩa aarutire mũriũ Isaaka kĩgongona-inĩ?
English: Wasn’t Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?

Kikuyu: Mũtigũkĩona atĩ wĩtĩkio wake nĩ warutire wĩra hamwe na ciĩko ciake, naguo wĩtĩkio wake ũgĩtuuo mũiganĩru kũna nĩ ũndũ wa ciĩko icio ciake.
English: You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was perfected.

Kikuyu: Namo Maandĩko makĩhingio marĩa moigĩte atĩrĩ, “Iburahĩmu agĩĩtĩkia Ngai, nakuo gwĩtĩkia kũu gũgĩtũma atuuo mũthingu,” nake agĩĩtwo mũrata wa Ngai.
English: So the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him as righteousness,” and he was called the friend of God.

Kikuyu: Nĩmũkuona atĩ mũndũ atuagwo mũthingu nĩ ũndũ wa ũrĩa ekaga, no ti ũndũ wa wĩtĩkio wiki.
English: You see then that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.

Kikuyu: O nake Rahabu ũrĩa warĩ mũmaraya-rĩ, githĩ ndaatuirwo mũthingu nĩ ũndũ wa ũrĩa eekire hĩndĩ ĩrĩa aanyiitire athigaani arĩa ũgeni na akĩmoonereria njĩra ĩngĩ ya kũũrĩra?
English: In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?

Kikuyu: O ta ũrĩa mwĩrĩ ũtarĩ na roho ũrĩ mũkuũ-rĩ, ũguo noguo wĩtĩkio ũtarĩ ciĩko ũrĩ mũkuũ.
English: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, ti aingĩ anyu magĩrĩirwo nĩ gũtuĩka arutani, tondũ nĩ mũũĩ atĩ ithuĩ arĩa tũrutanaga nĩtũgaatuĩrwo ituĩro rĩa hinya gũkĩra andũ arĩa angĩ.
English: Let not many of you be teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive heavier judgment.

Kikuyu: Ithuothe nĩtũhĩngĩcagwo nĩ maũndũ maingĩ. Mũndũ angĩkorwo ndarĩ na mahĩtia thĩinĩ wa maũndũ marĩa aragia-rĩ, ũcio nĩ mũkinyanĩru kũna, na nĩahotete kũriĩra mwĩrĩ wake wothe.
English: For we all stumble in many things. Anyone who doesn’t stumble in word is a perfect person, able to bridle the whole body also.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa twekĩra mbarathi mĩkwa tũnua nĩguo itwathĩkĩre-rĩ, nĩtũhotaga kũgarũra nyamũ ĩyo ĩrĩ yothe.
English: Indeed, we put bits into the horses’ mouths so that they may obey us, and we guide their whole body.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ ta rorai ũhoro wa marikabu ũrĩ ta kĩonereria. O na gũtuĩka nĩ nene na itwaragwo nĩ rũhuho rũrĩ na hinya-rĩ, nĩigarũragwo na gathukani kanini, ikarorio o kũrĩa mũtwarithia wacio ekwenda gũciroria.
English: Behold, the ships also, though they are so big and are driven by fierce winds, are yet guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires.

Kikuyu: Ũguo no taguo rũrĩmĩ rũhaana. Nĩ kĩĩga kĩnini kĩa mwĩrĩ, no nĩ rwĩĩkagĩrĩra mũno. Ta mwĩciiriei ũrĩa mũtitũ mũnene ũgwatagio mwaki nĩ gathandĩ o kanini.
English: So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!

Kikuyu: Ningĩ rũrĩmĩ nĩ mwaki, tondũ rũiyũrĩte mĩthemba yothe ya maũndũ ma waganu thĩinĩ wa ciĩga cia mwĩrĩ. Rũthũkagia mwĩrĩ wothe, rũkagwatia mwaki mũtũũrĩre wothe wa mũndũ, naruo rwene rũkoragwo rũmundĩtio mwaki nĩ Jehanamu.
English: And the tongue is a fire. The world of iniquity among our members is the tongue, which defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by Gehenna.

Kikuyu: Nyamũ cia mĩthemba yothe, na nyoni, na nyamũ iria itambaga thĩ, na nyamũ cia iria-inĩ rĩrĩa inene ciothe nĩihooreragio na cianahoorerio nĩ mũndũ,
English: For every kind of animal, bird, creeping thing, and sea creature is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind;

Kikuyu: no gũtirĩ mũndũ o na ũrĩkũ ũngĩhota kũhooreria rũrĩmĩ. Nĩruo kĩndũ kĩũru gĩtangĩkindĩria na rũiyũrĩtwo nĩ thumu wa kũũragana.
English: but nobody can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

Kikuyu: Tũgoocaga Mwathani, o we Ithe witũ, na rũrĩmĩ, na tũkaruma andũ naruo, o acio mombĩtwo marĩ na mũhianĩre wa Ngai.
English: With it we bless our God and Father, and with it we curse men who are made in the image of God.

Kikuyu: Kanua o kau-rĩ, no ko koimaga ũgooci na gakoima irumi. Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, ũguo tiguo kwagĩrĩire gũtuĩka.
English: Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.

Kikuyu: Kaĩ maaĩ mega na maaĩ ma cumbĩ mangĩtherũka kuuma gĩthima kĩmwe?
English: Does a spring send out from the same opening fresh and bitter water?

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, mũkũyũ no ũhote gũciara ndamaiyũ, kana mũthabibũ ũciare ngũyũ? O nakĩo gĩthima kĩa maaĩ ma cumbĩ gĩtingĩtherũka maaĩ mega.
English: Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine figs? Thus no spring yields both salt water and fresh water.

Kikuyu: Thĩinĩ wanyu-rĩ, nũũ ũrĩ na ũũgĩ na agataũkĩrwo nĩ maũndũ? Mũndũ ũcio nĩakĩonanie maũndũ macio na ũndũ wa mũtũũrĩre wake mwega, na ciĩko ciĩkĩĩtwo na njĩra ya kwĩnyiihia kũrĩa kuumanaga na ũũgĩ.
English: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom.

Kikuyu: No mũngĩkorwo ngoro-inĩ cianyu nĩ mũtũũragia ũiru na ũhoro wa kwenda kwĩyambatĩria- rĩ, mũtikae kwĩrahĩra ũndũ ũcio kana mũtuĩke a gũkaana ũhoro wa ma.
English: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth.

Kikuyu: “Ũũgĩ” ta ũcio tiguo ũikũrũkaga uumĩte igũrũ, no nĩ wa thĩ ĩno, na ti wa kĩĩroho, ũcio nĩ ũũgĩ wa mũcukani.
English: This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo harĩa harĩ na ũiru na ũhoro wa kwenda kwĩyambatĩria-rĩ, hau nĩho hakoragwo na ngũĩ na ciĩko ciothe cia waganu.
English: For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.

Kikuyu: No ũũgĩ ũrĩa uumaga igũrũ o mbere nĩ mũtheru; ningĩ nĩwendete thayũ, na nĩũcaayanagĩra, na nĩwĩnyiihagia, na nĩ ũiyũrĩtwo nĩ tha na maciaro mega, ningĩ ndũthutũkanagia, na ndũrĩ ũhinga.
English: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.

Kikuyu: Nao ateithũrani arĩa mahaandaga thayũ-rĩ, magethaga maciaro ma ũthingu.
English: Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩrĩ, nĩ kĩĩ gĩtũmaga kũgĩe na mbaara na ngũĩ thĩinĩ wanyu? Githĩ itiumaga merirĩria-inĩ manyu marĩa marũaga thĩinĩ wanyu?
English: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?

Kikuyu: Mwĩriragĩria kĩndũ no mũkaaga kũgĩa nakĩo. Ningĩ mũũraganaga na mũgacumĩkĩra, no mũtingĩhota kũgĩa na kĩrĩa mũkwenda. Mũtetanagia na mũkarũa. Mũgakĩaga kuona kĩndũ tondũ wa kwaga kũhooya Ngai.
English: You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa mwahooya-rĩ, nĩmwagaga kũheo, tondũ mũhooyaga mũrĩ na muoroto mũũru, tondũ mwendaga mũitangage kĩrĩa mwaheo na maũndũ ma gwĩkenia.
English: You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

Kikuyu: Inyuĩ atharania aya, kaĩ mũtooĩ atĩ kũgĩa ũrata na thĩ nĩ kũgĩa ũthũ na Ngai? Nĩ ũndũ ũcio mũndũ o wothe ũthuuraga kũgĩa ũrata na thĩ nĩkũgĩa ũthũ ya Ngai.
English: You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.

Kikuyu: Kana mũgwĩciiria Maandĩko maaragia ũhoro ũtarĩ na gĩtũmi, atĩ roho ũrĩa Ngai aatũmire ũtũũrage thĩinĩ witũ nĩ ũiguaga ũiru mũno?
English: Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain, “The Spirit who lives in us yearns jealously”?

Kikuyu: No nĩatũheaga wega wake makĩria. Kĩu nĩkĩo gĩtũmaga Maandĩko moige atĩrĩ: “Ngai nĩareganaga na arĩa etĩĩi no arĩa menyiihagia nĩo aheaga wega wake.”
English: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio mwĩnyiihagĩriei Ngai. Reganagai na mũcukani, nake nĩekũmũũrĩra.
English: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

Kikuyu: Kuhĩrĩriai Ngai, nake nĩekũmũkuhĩrĩria. Mwĩthambei moko manyu inyuĩ ehia, na mũtherie ngoro cianyu inyuĩ andũ a ngoro igĩrĩ.
English: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.

Kikuyu: Iguai kĩeha, mũcakae, na mũgirĩke. Garũrai mĩtheko yanyu ĩtuĩke macakaya, nakĩo gĩkeno kĩanyu kĩgarũrũke gĩtuĩke kĩeha.
English: Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.

Kikuyu: Mwĩnyiihĩriei Mwathani, nake nĩekũmũtũũgĩria.
English: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, tigai gũcambania mũndũ na ũrĩa ũngĩ. Ũrĩa wothe waragia ũhoro wa gũcambia mũrũ kana mwarĩ wa ithe kana akamũtuĩra ciira-rĩ, nĩ watho acambagia na akaũtuĩra ciira. Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa ũgũtuĩra watho ciira-rĩ, ndũkoragwo ũkĩhingia watho, no ũkoragwo ũrĩ mũtuanĩri ciira.
English: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.

Kikuyu: Kũrĩ Mũheani wa watho, na Mũtuanĩri ciira o ũmwe, o we ũrĩa ũrĩ na ũhoti wa kũhonokia na kũniinana. No wee-rĩ, ũkĩrĩ ũ nĩguo ũtuĩre mũndũ ũrĩa ũngĩ ciira?
English: Only one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?

Kikuyu: Rĩu ta thikĩrĩriai, inyuĩ mugaga atĩrĩ: “Ũmũthĩ kana rũciũ nĩtũgũthiĩ itũũra rĩna tũikare kuo mwaka ũmwe, tũrute wĩra wa wonjoria kuo, tũgĩe na mbeeca.”
English: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.”

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, inyuĩ mũtiũĩ ũrĩa gũgaatuĩka rũciũ. Muoyo wanyu ũkĩrĩ kĩ? Inyuĩ mũrĩ o kĩbii kĩrĩa kĩonekaga o kahinda kanini, gĩgacooka gĩgathira biũ.
English: Yet you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. For what is your life? For you are a vapor that appears for a little time and then vanishes away.

Kikuyu: Handũ ha ũguo-rĩ, mwagĩrĩirwo nĩ kugaga atĩrĩ, “Mwathani angĩenda-rĩ, nĩ tũgũtũũra muoyo na twĩkage ũndũ ũyũ na ũyũ.”
English: For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”

Kikuyu: No rĩu inyuĩ nĩ kwĩraha mwĩrahaga mũrĩ na nguthi. Mwĩraho ta ũcio wothe nĩ mũũru.
English: But now you glory in your boasting. All such boasting is evil.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ wa ũguo, mũndũ wothe ũũĩ gwĩka wega na ndekaga-rĩ, ũcio nĩ kwĩhia ehagia.
English: To him therefore who knows to do good and doesn’t do it, to him it is sin.

Kikuyu: Rĩu ta thikĩrĩriai, inyuĩ itonga ici, rĩrai na mũgirĩke tondũ wa mathĩĩna marĩa maramũkora.
English: Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming on you.

Kikuyu: Ũtonga wanyu nĩ ũbuthĩte, nacio nguo cianyu nĩ ndĩe nĩ memenyi.
English: Your riches are corrupted and your garments are moth-eaten.

Kikuyu: Thahabu na betha cianyu nĩ irootete. Kũroota gwacio nĩ ũira wa atĩ nĩireganĩte na inyuĩ, na nĩikũrĩa mĩĩrĩ yanyu imũniine o ta mwaki. Inyuĩ mwĩigĩire mũthithũ mũingĩ wa matukũ ma kũrigĩrĩria.
English: Your gold and your silver are corroded, and their corrosion will be for a testimony against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have laid up your treasure in the last days.

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩrĩ! Mĩcaara ĩrĩa mwaregire kũrĩha aruti a wĩra arĩa maamũrĩmĩire mĩgũnda nĩĩramũkaĩra. Gũkaya kwa arĩa maamũgetheire irio nĩgũkinyĩire matũ ma Mwathani Mwene hinya wothe.
English: Behold, the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you have kept back by fraud, cry out; and the cries of those who reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Armies.

Kikuyu: Mũtũũrĩte gũkũ thĩ na mĩago na mũgĩĩkenagia. Inyuĩ mwĩnoretie nĩ ũndũ wa mũthenya wa gũthĩnjwo.
English: You have lived in luxury on the earth, and taken your pleasure. You have nourished your hearts as in a day of slaughter.

Kikuyu: Inyuĩ nĩ mũtuĩrĩire andũ ciira na mũkamooraga matarĩ na mahĩtia, o acio matarĩ ũũru na inyuĩ.
English: You have condemned and you have murdered the righteous one. He doesn’t resist you.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, kiragĩrĩriai, o nginya rĩrĩa Mwathani agooka. Ta rorai ũrĩa mũrĩmi etagĩrĩra mũgũnda wake ũrute irio iria irĩ bata, na agakirĩrĩria nginya ciurĩrwo nĩ mbura ya mbere o na ya keerĩ ategũthethũka.
English: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain.

Kikuyu: O na inyuĩ-rĩ, kirĩrĩriai na mwĩhaande wega, tondũ Mwathani arĩ hakuhĩ gũũka.
English: You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, tigagai gũtetania, nĩgeetha mũtikanatuĩrwo ciira. Mũtuanĩri ciira arũngiĩ o mũrango-inĩ!
English: Don’t grumble, brothers, against one another, so that you won’t be judged. Behold, the judge stands at the door.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, mwĩrutei na maũndũ marĩa mooru anabii meekirwo, o acio maaragia thĩinĩ wa rĩĩtwa rĩa Mwathani, naguo ũhoro ũcio ũtuĩke kĩonereria kĩanyu gĩa gũkirĩrĩria rĩrĩa mũkũnyamario.
English: Take, brothers, for an example of suffering and of perseverance, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

Kikuyu: O ta ũrĩa mũũĩ, acio maakirĩrĩirie-rĩ, tũmatuaga arathime. Nĩmũiguĩte ũhoro wa gũkirĩrĩria kwa Ayubu, na nĩmuonete ũrĩa Mwathani eekire marigĩrĩrio-inĩ. Mwathani aiyũrĩtwo nĩ ũtugi na tha.
English: Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the Lord in the outcome, and how the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, igũrũ rĩa maũndũ mothe-rĩ, tigagai kwĩhĩta. Mũtikanehĩte na igũrũ kana na thĩ, o na kana na kĩndũ kĩngĩ o na kĩ. Inyuĩ-rĩ, mwoiga “Ĩĩ” nĩĩtuĩke ĩĩ, na mwoiga “Aca” nĩĩtuĩke aca, nĩguo mũtikae gũtuĩrwo ciira.
English: But above all things, my brothers, don’t swear—not by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your “yes” be “yes”, and your “no”, “no”, so that you don’t fall into hypocrisy.

Kikuyu: Nĩ harĩ mũndũ thĩinĩ wanyu wonete ũũru? Ũcio nĩahooe. Nĩ harĩ mũndũ ũkenete? Ũcio nĩaine nyĩmbo cia kũgooca.
English: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.

Kikuyu: Nĩ harĩ mũndũ thĩinĩ wanyu mũrũaru? Ũcio nĩete athuuri a kanitha mamũhooere na mamũhake maguta thĩinĩ wa rĩĩtwa rĩa Mwathani.
English: Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord;

Kikuyu: Namo mahooya mangĩhooywo na wĩtĩkio nĩ megũtũma mũndũ ũcio mũrũaru ahone; Mwathani nĩekũmwarahũra. Angĩkorwo ehĩtie- rĩ, nĩekũrekerwo mehia make.
English: and the prayer of faith will heal him who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio umbũranagĩrai mehia manyu o mũndũ na ũrĩa ũngĩ, na mũhooyanagĩre nĩgeetha mũhonagio. Ihooya rĩa mũndũ mũthingu nĩ rĩrĩ hinya na nĩ rĩtũmaga maũndũ manene mekĩke.
English: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.

Kikuyu: Elija aarĩ mũndũ o ta ithuĩ. Nake nĩahooire Ngai na kĩyo atĩ mbura ndĩkoire, nayo mbura ndĩoirire bũrũri-inĩ ũcio ihinda rĩa mĩaka ĩtatũ na nuthu.
English: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ agĩcooka akĩhooya, nakuo matu-inĩ gũkiuma mbura, nayo thĩ ĩgĩciara maciaro mayo.
English: He prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩrĩ ariũ na aarĩ a Ithe witũ, mũndũ ũmwe wanyu angĩagaga oime ũhoro-inĩ wa ma nake mũndũ ũngĩ amũgarũre-rĩ,
English: Brothers, if any among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,

Kikuyu: ririkanai ũũ: Mũndũ ũrĩa wothe ũgarũraga mwĩhia kuuma njĩra-inĩ yake njũru-rĩ, nĩkũmũhonokia akaamũhonokia kuuma harĩ gĩkuũ na ahumbĩre mehia maingĩ.
English: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
